text:
Vitali Pinchuk had waited a long time for his first NHL goal, and it came on a backhand in the first period of a game Nashville ended up winning in overtime. Pinchuk was never drafted. He came over after a 66-point season in the KHL with Dinamo Minsk, and his goal put the Predators up 2-1. Steven Stamkos finished the night on a power-play slap shot 2:18 into overtime, giving NSH a 3-2 win at Ball Arena and its third straight victory.

The Avalanche have a case that they were the better team on the shot chart. COL attempted 77 shots to NSH's 51 and held the edge in expected goals (the quality of chances) at even strength, 2.31 to 2.08. But Nashville produced more total expected goals, 3.53 to 3.19, and our deserved-to-win number, the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins, gave NSH 56 percent. Justus Annunen stopped 30 of 32 shots, about 1.2 goals better than the chances against him warranted, while Mackenzie Blackwood saved 22 of 25 and was roughly half a goal better than expected. Nashville also blocked 25 shots to Colorado's 10.

Parker Kelly tied it at 2-2 early in the second period, a goal he scored on a 16 percent chance, and it stayed that way through regulation. For Nashville, the win extends a run that included a 6-2 victory over this same Colorado team on Oct. 25. For the Avalanche, a night of heavy volume and little to show for it means they'll want those chances to turn into goals next time out.
